suggested_titles.academic: The 93-Year Floor: Exponential Decay of Lifespan in the Genesis Genealogies and the Thermodynamic Limit of Common Grace
suggested_titles.provocative: The Number That Shouldn't Be There: Why the Bible's Lifespan Data Fits a Decay Curve with a Floor at 93 Years

opening_analysis.diagnosis: The opening is strong: it immediately establishes a data-first, no-interpretation stance that builds credibility and curiosity. The thesis (the lifespan data fits an exponential decay with a floor around 93 years) is visible by paragraph 2. The problem (the dramatic drop after the Flood) is stated in paragraph 1. The opening could be improved by hinting at the theological stakes earlier to hook readers who might otherwise see it as a dry data exercise.

unresolved_tensions: The model finds 93, Moses says 70-80, modern data says 73. The paper treats these as converging, but the discrepancy between 93 and 70-80 is not fully resolved—only attributed to 'measuring slightly different things at slightly different times.'

missing_bridges: Between Section II (the curve) and Section III (why exponential), a brief transition explaining why the reader should care about the functional form would help.
redundant_passages: The phrase 'Something is holding the floor' appears in Section IV and again in the conclusion—slightly redundant.
flow.suggested_reorder: No major reordering needed. The structure is logical: data, curve, mechanism, interpretation, conclusion.

paragraph_function_map.main_point: Start with the numbers, not interpretation.
The data is specific and has been sitting in Genesis for millennia.
The curve will be discussed after the data.
Genesis gives specific ages, not approximations.
Pre-Flood lifespans are in the 900s.
Post-Flood lifespans drop dramatically.
Something happened at the Flood, and it happened fast.
The exponential decay model is introduced.
The model finds a floor at 93 years without being told about Psalm 90.
Psalm 90:10 says 70-80 years.
Modern average life expectancy is about 73 years.
Three independent measurements converge on the same floor.
The floor is real and points to a physical reality.
The data is a measurement record, not mythology.
Why exponential and not linear?
Linear decay is gradual erosion.
Exponential decay is compounding.
The exponential shape is the signature of generational entropy.
The Flood resets some accumulation but not all.
The data is a record of generational entropy, not mythology.

rearrangement_suggestions: Move the paragraph starting 'Now here's the thing I want you to sit with' (paragraph 9) to immediately after the table to strengthen the hook.
Consider moving Section III (Why Exponential) before Section II (The Curve) to establish the framework before presenting the fit.
Cut the redundant 'Something is holding the floor' in the conclusion—already stated in Section IV.
top_3_fixes: Resolve the discrepancy between the model's 93 and Moses' 70-80 more explicitly—currently hand-waved as 'measuring slightly different things.'
Add a transition sentence between Section II and Section III to explain why the functional form matters before diving into it.
Strengthen the conclusion by tying the floor more directly to the theological claim about common grace, rather than repeating earlier phrases.
